title: Memory contract (rizzstack.memory/1)
description: The parsed frontmatter of one memory document in the rizzstack memory vault. A memory is a markdown file with YAML frontmatter; this record is what that frontmatter parses to. The vault is semantic memory distilled from work, never raw transcripts: sources name where every claim came from, the digest guards every write against concurrent editors, and the retention block states how the memory expires. The operation envelopes a vault service accepts (write, query, brief injection) live under $defs. This file is the workflow-repo mirror of the umbrella protocol row; see docs/memory-contract.md and docs/protocol.md.

schema.description: The contract version. Every memory carries it, so a reader can tell what it is looking at before reading anything else.

id.description: Stable lowercase kebab slug, unique across the whole vault. Renaming is refused; supersession replaces a memory instead.

type.description: decision: a chosen direction and why. learning: a durable insight about how work behaves. pitfall: a confirmed trap and its fix. env-fact: a checked fact about a concrete thing in the environment (a host, a service, a repo, a tool). project-state: where a project stands and what is next. reference: stable external or distilled reference material with a re-verify deadline.

created.description: RFC 3339 instant the memory was created. Never after modified.

modified.description: RFC 3339 instant of the last accepted edit.

policy.description: The expiry policy. The policy names the duty: who sets expires or superseded_by, and when. It is fixed per type by the implications below.

expires.description: The deadline after which the memory stops being served, or null while the policy has not set one. A decision and a learning never set it; a reference must.

superseded_by.description: The id of the memory that replaced this one, or null. Setting it expires this memory and keeps the trail.

kind.description: What kind of evidence the claim came from. A session-digest is the distilled summary of a work session, never the raw transcript.

ref.description: Where the source lives: a vault-relative path, a pull-request id, a file path, or an external locator. Not the content itself.

note.description: Already-scrubbed free text about what this source contributed. No private URLs, hostnames, addresses or file contents.

sources.description: Provenance: where every claim in the body came from. A memory with no source is refused; a raw transcript is never a source by itself, only a distilled digest of one is.

sha.description: Digest of this memory: sha256 over the canonical JSON of the frontmatter without the sha field itself (sorted keys, compact separators), then a newline, then the markdown body. A write whose expected digest is stale is refused with a re-read requirement.

grant_ref.description: Locator of the durable approval record that authorized this write outside the writer's own subtree.

approved_by.description: Who approved the grant, as a kind-prefixed id. Writers cannot approve their own grants; curated zones require a human approver.

authority.description: The explicit authorization a write carries when it targets anything outside the writer's own quarantine subtree. Null means the write must stay inside that subtree.

writer.description: Who is writing, as a kind-prefixed id. It selects the writer's own quarantine subtree.

path.description: Vault-relative markdown target. No absolute paths and no dot segments; the vault service also resolves it inside the vault root.

body.description: The markdown body, starting with the level-1 title line. The digest in memory.sha must match this body.

expected_sha.description: The digest the writer last read, or null for a create. A mismatch with the stored digest is refused as sha_conflict with the current digest and a re-read requirement.

code.description: none when accepted; otherwise the named refusal rule.

reread_required.description: True exactly for sha_conflict: the writer must re-read the memory and reapply its edit on the current digest.

current_sha.description: The stored digest at refusal time, when one exists, so the writer can re-read against it.

log_seq.description: The receipt sequence in log.md, on acceptance.

write-result.description: What a write returns: an accepted receipt, or a refusal with a code, an optional current digest and the re-read requirement.

q.description: The natural-language or keyword query text.

mode.description: Requested retrieval engine. When an engine is unavailable the vault falls down the chain: hybrid or semantic to keyword (the FTS5 index) to grep (ripgrep over the files plus the index and wikilinks). mode_used in the result says what actually ran.

include_expired.description: False hides expired memories; audit paths may opt in.

mode_used.description: The engine that actually ran. Hybrid fuses the keyword and embedding rankings with reciprocal rank fusion; it never runs silently degraded without saying so.

vault_rev.description: The vault generation or revision the result was computed against.

sha.description: Digest of the hit at result time; a consumer re-reading the file can detect drift.

score.description: Retrieval score after fusion or fallback ranking.

snippet.description: A short verbatim excerpt for display.

hits.description: Ranked hits. Expired memories are hidden unless the query opted in.

sha.description: Digest of the memory the excerpt was taken from, pinned at injection time.

path.description: Vault-relative path, so a worker can pull the full memory when it needs more.

excerpt.description: The size-capped excerpt carried into the brief.

items.description: Typed, digest-pinned, size-capped memory excerpts for one brief. Empty is honest: a brief with nothing relevant carries none.

caps.description: The caps actually applied. They must not exceed the contract defaults of 8 items, 480 characters per excerpt and 4000 characters in total.

vault_rev.description: The vault generation the excerpts were pinned against.

injection.description: The memory-context block a dispatch brief carries in the lease payload. Built by the recall step before dispatch; never assembled by the worker itself.
